## Kubernetes scope removal

Removes cluster operational APIs/UI, discovery/provider adapters, metric projections, SDK dependency, fixtures and dedicated provisioning CI. Retained Kubernetes sources can no longer be re-enabled/relabelled or used with otherwise valid HTTP collectors. Nested/aliased operational configurations are rejected at input, template attachment, activation and persisted-state execution boundaries; queued/leased work is retired without deleting history.

Legacy tables, immutable decisions, tenant fences and applied migrations remain intact. VM/EC2, APIs, read-only Pentaho and generic telemetry labels remain supported. No production/UAT access, collector upgrade, unrelated durability remediation, deployment or merge.

The collector screen and creation source selector also exclude retained legacy identities; browser acceptance requires a visible supported collector as a positive control.

## Closure acceptance

Tested product/fixture SHA: `402834e351d816d48760974e4566185631600995`.
Final evidence commit: `ec9c712a22db9bc46e101edafcc2f5e09b165025` (documentation only after tested source).

- Full PostgreSQL backend suite: **547 passed, 2 skipped, 0 failures/errors** (549 total).
- Frontend: **38 passed**; lint/build passed.
- Full existing HTTP/browser release harness: **13 grouped gates passed**, including **67 focused HTTP assertions** and **17 focused Chromium assertion groups**, plus existing CRUD, pagination, tenant/RBAC, telemetry, alerts, incidents, retention and TLS checks.
- Fresh migrations, populated upgrade, dump/restore and per-table content hashes passed. Full HTTP fixture restored **100 tables / 1,116 rows / 499 constraints**. Legacy hashes unchanged after attempted retired association mutations.
- Final owned container/process/network cleanup recorded. Failed attempts, screenshots, command exit codes and raw logs are preserved.

Evidence: [final acceptance matrix](https://github.com/Parikshit-Sahrawat/OpsControl_Dashboard/blob/ec9c712a22db9bc46e101edafcc2f5e09b165025/docs/verification/scope-removal/kubernetes-platforms/FINAL_ACCEPTANCE_MATRIX.md), with browser, HTTP, semantic-audit, preservation reports and SHA-256 manifests beside it.

All 15 hosted CI checks passed at final commit `ec9c712a22db9bc46e101edafcc2f5e09b165025`. The closure comment records exact job links and results; no earlier SHA checks are substituted.

## Review limits — remain draft

All four requested removal workstreams have passing local evidence; independent owner acceptance remains required. Two unchanged pinned collector-binary checks are NOT TESTED. Synthetic configuration/provider fixtures are not genuine-provider certification or independent UAT. Physical in-flight worker draining and large-fleet scheduler benchmarking are not claimed.

The legacy auxiliary EKS ledger has a pre-existing trailing-literal-newline serialization defect; original bytes are retained as raw text, while new canonical acceptance ledgers are valid JSON. Older pre-fix exploratory anonymous volumes cannot all be conclusively attributed; the known failed-run volume was removed, final fixtures use tmpfs, and no broad cleanup was attempted. Destructive legacy schema retirement still requires separately approved export, retention, relationship and recovery review.

**CHK-001 FAIL · CHK-002 BLOCKED · SECURITY BLOCKED · RELEASE NO-GO.**

## Development consolidation decision — 2026-10-10

Owner approved merging into `main` as the development baseline after passing automated checks. Live AWS and genuine Pentaho Carte acceptance are deferred follow-up work. Earlier no-merge statements below record the previous hold and are superseded by this decision; production deployment is not part of this merge.

## Secure remote HTTP monitoring (Phase 2 implementation)

**Security boundary:** Agent-initiated outbound HTTPS to control plane; **no inbound path** from OpsControl to private targets. Draft feature; no production deploy or merge.

### Implemented
- PostgreSQL migrations 0015/0016: tenant-scoped remote job/evidence tables and explicit collector→worker binding.
- Platform-admin routes for worker exact-host/CIDR policy, assignment/unassignment, manual idempotent dispatch and job status.
- Trusted scheduler process auto-dispatches due assigned remote HTTP collectors; legacy local scheduler explicitly skips remote-owned collectors.
- Worker-scoped outbound poll/claim with `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`, random 90-second lease nonce, max 3 attempts and exhausted-lease expiry.
- Evidence endpoint rejects anonymous/human/wrong-org/wrong-assignment/invalid nonce/expired timestamp, unknown fields, oversized JSON and event replay; one evidence row per job, transactional CollectorRun, compatible MetricSample and native Alert Rule evaluation.
- Remote agent has independent mandatory local egress policy that the server cannot widen: HTTPS GET/443, exact FQDN, strict CIDR allowlists, all DNS A/AAAA answers validated, IP-pinned TLS hostname verification, no redirects, no request credentials, no response body capture and metadata/link-local/loopback denial.
- Staleness marker when monitoring evidence stops; sanitized monitoring errors.
- CI tests: egress SSRF/DNS rebinding/local policy; disposable PostgreSQL two-tenant auth, work claim, auto scheduler, forged/replayed evidence, metric and alert path; frontend build; dependency/Git history scan.
- Documentation: `docs/REMOTE_AGENT_QUICKSTART.md` and security checklist.

### Release hold
- Full latest-head CI and independent code/security review are required. Agent Python restrictions **do not replace** OS/container/network-layer egress firewalling.
- Browser synthetics, AWS/K8s/Apache deep collectors, secret-provider integration and secure authenticated app journeys remain separate. Only unauthenticated HTTPS GET/status HTTP probing is implemented in this slice.
- Production TLS ingress, trust/rotation policy, private CA testing, load/HA, storage retention and org-wide security sign-off remain tracked in issue #18.

**Dependency:** This draft PR is stacked on security PR #19, itself stacked on #17. Nothing in `main` is modified.
title: feat: private-network remote agent — authenticated scheduled jobs, evidence and egress controls

Customer resource ownership and internal access administration need separate models. This change retains customer `organizations` and their resource FKs, adds provider-owned departments and employee memberships, and enforces explicit role/customer permissions across backend services and the UI.

- Additive migration **0025** preserves user/customer/resource UUIDs, password hashes and sessions. Legacy customer memberships remain compatibility grants; unknown legacy roles abort transactionally. Unsafe schema downgrade is refused.
- Default-deny RBAC pairs role and customer grants, supports employee restrictions, checks current rights on every request, protects self/inactive/DENY authorization paths, last platform administrator and reserved administration credentials/lifecycle, and audits administrative success/denial.
- Employees, Departments, Roles & Permissions, Customer Access and Access Audit provide functional forms, filters, paging, inherited/direct previews and confirmation. The operational selector contains authorized customers and is hidden on both administration pages; malformed cached selections are discarded.
- Worker customer/job/lease authorization, protected local provider execution and shared template administration retain their separate trust boundaries.
- **Full PostgreSQL schema reconciliation:** models now match all existing migration-defined indexes, uniqueness constraints, JSONB types and template-version cascade behavior. All **32 previous drift groups are resolved**, without a new migration, destructive DDL or data changes. Full metadata comparison and real `alembic check` are enforced in populated-fixture and rebuilt-Docker CI gates. Six additional tests protect index predicates/order and schema semantics.

Validation at **d96eb77145466b6ab1d5d8f2c56dc19ddfceb160**: **35 backend cases**, 4 frontend cases and production build; 25 real HTTP/PostgreSQL security groups; 7 actual Chromium journeys; clean Docker build/bootstrap/restart with zero-drift image-level Alembic check; full HTTP/ETL/incident/all-tab dark/light regressions; release worker/resilience/TLS/retention and populated restore (51 tables, 913 rows, 190 constraints). All 50 application tables have zero schema/model differences and zero invalid indexes. Redacted evidence and tested source hashes are committed. Local networking labs run sequentially.

**Remote CI:** All 18 checks passed for `d96eb77145466b6ab1d5d8f2c56dc19ddfceb160`, including full-schema/access acceptance, Docker, operational dashboards, monitoring, security and release regressions.

The legacy staging gate tests reversible pre-access migrations before its populated 0016→0025 upgrade, with explicit refusal for production/non-loopback or already-upgraded access databases.

**Acceptance ownership and limits:** The owner accepts the single-provider runtime and is conducting independent security review and UAT locally; automated fixtures do not certify those reviews. Deployed scale, recovery objectives and genuine provider acceptance remain separately recorded release gates. This reconciliation needs no production deployment or production data modification; neither was performed. The PR remains unmerged for review.

[Complete implementation report and exact Docker verification](https://github.com/Parikshit-Sahrawat/OpsControl_Dashboard/blob/d96eb77145466b6ab1d5d8f2c56dc19ddfceb160/docs/architecture/ACCESS_IMPLEMENTATION_REPORT.md) · [Architecture and rollback](https://github.com/Parikshit-Sahrawat/OpsControl_Dashboard/blob/d96eb77145466b6ab1d5d8f2c56dc19ddfceb160/docs/architecture/CUSTOMER_DEPARTMENT_RBAC.md) · [All 32 schema differences and resolutions](https://github.com/Parikshit-Sahrawat/OpsControl_Dashboard/blob/d96eb77145466b6ab1d5d8f2c56dc19ddfceb160/docs/architecture/SCHEMA_MODEL_RECONCILIATION.md)
